title: Corporate Hedging Strategies, Lessons from Corporate Disasters (P&G, Orange County, Metallgesellschaft, Hammersmith & Fulham), and Best Practices
prerequisites: Derivative instruments (swaps, futures, options) and hedging mechanics
Corporate treasury management and risk governance basics
Margin calls, liquidity risk, and roll yields
learningOutcomes: Distinguish corporate hedging from speculation and evaluate treasury departments as cost centers ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Analyze historical corporate derivative disasters (Procter & Gamble, Orange County, Metallgesellschaft, Hammersmith & Fulham) ([fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06]).
Manage liquidity risk independently from accounting solvency and maintain cash buffers for margin calls ([fact-07]).
Apply net economic profit invariants, prohibit leveraged exotics, and enforce rigorous multi-factor stress testing ([fact-08], [fact-09], [fact-10]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Evaluating treasurers as profit centers creates a perverse incentive to enter leveraged, asymmetric exotic derivatives that risk catastrophic corporate failure to save modest upfront borrowing costs ([fact-02]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: As Metallgesellschaft demonstrated, shifting market structures from backwardation to contango generate negative roll yields and massive daily exchange margin calls that can drain corporate liquidity entirely ([fact-05]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Liquidity risk must be decoupled from paper accounting solvency; solvent institutions can be forced into emergency liquidation if they lack liquid cash reserves to satisfy intra-day margin calls ([fact-07]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Treasurer Robert Citron leveraged Orange County's $7.5 billion investment pool into over $20 billion in nominal holdings using reverse repurchase (repo) agreements to purchase inverse floaters. When the Fed raised rates 300 bps in 1994, repo lenders demanded $1.7 billion in collateral.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What was the ultimate financial outcome for Orange County? 2) Why must corporate treasuries operate strictly as cost centers rather than profit centers?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: Corporate hedging must strictly isolate operating exposures, and treasuries must operate as cost centers rather than speculative profit centers ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Historical disasters like P&G, Orange County, and Metallgesellschaft highlight the dangers of leverage, repo borrowing, and contango roll drains ([fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05]).
Sound treasury governance requires decoupling liquidity from solvency, prohibiting leveraged exotics, and enforcing rigorous 30-day stress tests ([fact-07], [fact-09], [fact-10]).
